name: Chicago
originNote: Chicago Midway, midpoint of runway 13L/31R, from FAA runway geometry.
Midway rather than O'Hare for the same reason New York uses LaGuardia: the
origin wants to be near the city being flown over, not twenty-seven kilometres
out in the suburbs. O'Hare sits comfortably inside the region either way.
extentNote: The same 30 nm half-width as New York, so the LOD rings and §7's spacing rules carry over without a second set of numbers.

tiers.note: Centred between the Loop, O'Hare and Midway, which is the ground actually flown.
Everything else, including the coarse LOD ring that reaches past the map edge.

airfieldTier.note: Every airfield the tiers above do not reach gets its own 60 m tier. About 20 KB each.

surface.note: As New York. Chicago needs it more, not less: the region has about 25 m of relief in total, so land cover is doing essentially all the visual work.

buildings.note: The same cut as New York, kept deliberately rather than tuned per region — a threshold that moves per city is a threshold nobody can reason about.

waterNote: Chicago has no coastline. `natural=coastline` is for the sea, and the Great
Lakes are mapped as ordinary water polygons — Lake Michigan is one relation
tagged natural=water, water=lake. So the coastline assembly finds nothing here
and the region falls back to land-everywhere, after which the inland-water
layer paints the lake. This is the path New York never exercised, and building
Chicago is how the builder gets tested as a tool rather than as a script that
happened to produce one good file.
